title: Wheelwright v5 Verification Objects
description: Phase 4 schema for the v5 verification object family (docs/wheelwright-v5-control-plane-directive.md S10-S15). Built ALONGSIDE the v4 prose-verify-block-on-a-lug convention. Nothing in the running v4 harness reads or writes this shape yet — see Part IV Doctrine 2 (strangler cutover: fully old or fully new, flipped by a recorded transition receipt, no dual-read window). Three independently-addressable object kinds share this file, discriminated by `object_type`: `verification` (S10/S11/S12), `validation_setup` (S13), `execution_result` (S14).

model_provider_ref.description: The model+provider that performed an attributed action (directive S28).

attribution.description: Durable attribution (directive S28), mirroring lug-v5.schema.json's attribution shape.

legacy_provenance.description: Migration provenance (directive S37). Present whenever this object originated from a v4 verify block rather than native v5 creation.

raw_v4_verify.description: The v4 verify content preserved verbatim, unmodified — never reinterpreted or fabricated into a command (directive S37 + Phase-4 honesty rule).

unknown_fields.description: Names of v5 fields that could not be populated from the v4 source and were marked legacy/unknown rather than fabricated.

coverage_target.description: One unit of work a verification object covers (directive S10). A verification is not owned by the thing it verifies — coverage is a reference, not containment.

kind.description: What shape of work this reference points at (directive S10).

ref.description: Identifier of the covered work — a lug id, initiative id, feature-area name, suite name, behavior name, or regression-class name.

schedule_entry.description: One maintenance schedule attached to a verification, with the trigger list that schedule implies (directive S12). The canonical default trigger list per kind lives in verification_objects.py:SCHEDULE_TRIGGERS; `triggers` here may narrow or extend it explicitly.

triggers.description: Concrete events that fire this schedule, e.g. 'source_file_changed', 'daily_cron', 'release_cut'.

executability.description: Phase-4 honesty rule: whether this verification names a real, machine-executable oracle. A prose-only verify block MUST NOT be marked EXECUTABLE just because it was moved into this schema (Doctrine 1: admission by evidence, not declaration).

oracle.description: The machine-executable check this verification runs. Required when executability=EXECUTABLE; absent when UNEXECUTABLE (no oracle is ever fabricated for prose).

commands.description: Literal, runnable command strings. Each one is either authored natively or carried forward verbatim from a v4 verify item that was already an executable oracle — never synthesized from prose.

retention_policy.description: Directive S15: durable definitions persist forever; recent evidence stays detailed; older evidence compresses to aggregates; expired evidence is deleted or archived by policy. This object configures the thresholds; verification_objects.py:apply_retention() is the pure function that enforces them over execution_result evidence. Never applies to the verification/validation_setup definitions themselves.

hot_days.description: Evidence younger than this stays in full detail.

aggregate_after_days.description: Evidence at/after this age is compressed into an aggregate summary.

expire_after_days.description: Evidence at/after this age is archived or deleted per archive_on_expire.

archive_on_expire.description: True: expired evidence is archived (metadata-only record kept). False: expired evidence is deleted outright. Default policy-dependent — always explicit, never implied.

verification.description: Directive S10/S11/S12: an independently addressable verification object. May cover one or many lugs, an initiative, a feature area, a suite, a behavior, or a regression class. Not owned by the thing it verifies.

coverage.description: Directive S11: explicit, measurable coverage. Coverage that cannot be queried is not coverage — this array is exactly what verification_objects.py:compute_coverage() reads.

schedule.description: Directive S12. Absent/empty means no standing maintenance schedule is attached (e.g. a one-off migrated MANUAL-only record still populates this — see migrate_v4_verify).

validation_setup_ref.description: Directive S13: reference to the reusable validation_setup object this verification runs against, by id + the specific version a run must use.

unexecutable_reason.description: Required (enforced by verification_objects.py, not schema alone since it is conditional) when executability=UNEXECUTABLE. States plainly why no oracle exists — e.g. 'migrated v4 verify block is prose, not a command; no oracle fabricated'.

oracle.description: Present iff executability=EXECUTABLE (conditional requirement enforced in verification_objects.py).

legacy.description: Present iff this record was produced by migrate_v4_verify(). Absent on natively-created v5 verification objects.

validation_setup.description: Directive S13: validation_setup is a first-class reusable object — seed data, relational records, fixtures, environment, auth state, dependencies, cleanup. Not duplicated test prose; runs reference this by id+version.

version.description: Bumped whenever the setup's contents materially change; execution_result.setup_used.setup_version pins a run to exactly this.

dependencies.description: Other validation_setup ids (and versions, encoded 'id@version') this setup composes on top of.

cleanup.description: Teardown/cleanup steps this setup requires after a run.

execution_result.description: Directive S14: an attributable child result produced by actually running a verification. Records what ran, its trigger, the setup used, the version tested, timing, resources, result, evidence, and any failures discovered.

verification_id.description: The verification object this is a result of.

trigger.description: Which concrete trigger fired this run (one entry from the owning verification's schedule.triggers, or 'operator_invoked'/'MANUAL').

schedule_kind.description: Which schedule kind this run's trigger belongs to, if any.

setup_used.description: Directive S13: which validation_setup VERSION this run actually used. Absent when the verification has no validation_setup_ref.

version_tested.description: The revision/build/lug-version under test, e.g. a git sha.

resources.description: Resource accounting for the run (tokens, cost, cpu_seconds, etc.) — freeform, provider-defined keys.

result.description: UNEXECUTABLE is the only legal result for a run against an executability=UNEXECUTABLE verification — such a run can never report PASS (Phase-4 honesty rule).

evidence.description: Raw evidence for this run: logs, output, links, artifacts. Freeform; retention compresses this field for aged records (directive S15).

failures_discovered.description: Structured records of any failures this run surfaced, feeding directive S34 rework.
